setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (4 reviews): Reviewer picks The Other One as the show's highlight, praising the jamming and Phil's playing; The Other One is called fireworks throughout, among the tour's best alongside the 4/26 version [3][4][7][11]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 other source): China Cat Sunflower segues into I Know You Rider [1]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): The He's Gone from this night was chosen for the Europe '72 album release [4]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Truckin' leads into a powerful Other One that wanders widely [6]
- **Me And Bobby McGee** (1 review): Mellow melodic noodling in the Other One settles into Me and Bobby McGee, then returns to the Other One [6]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): The Other One finally fades into Wharf Rat [6]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Sugar Magnolia and Not Fade Away as power-packed [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **Two Souls In Communion**: rare: 10 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd72-05-10.sbd.kaplan.1582.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 31 songs; 212 min; rated 4.79/5 by 19 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording is weaker than the May 4, 1972 Paris show, and the tape may run slightly fast; Sound is very good, with slight tape sound audible in quieter passages; Sound is superb with a lively mix and excellent instrument separation [10][12][13]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the band seems to play especially well whenever they perform in the Netherlands [2]
- Quotes Dennis McNally describing Amsterdam's Concertgebouw as a jewel of a theater [13]
- Reviewer ranks this show and the following night's among the band's very best performances [3]
- The show is overshadowed by the masterpiece played the next night, 5/11 [4]
- Reviewer says it is overshadowed by Rotterdam and may hold the tour's best Other One [5]
- Reviewer says the next night's show is even better [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-05-10.sbd.kaplan.1582.sbeok.shnf**: source: S:MR > Cassette > DAT > CDR > SHN [1]. Also: Soundboard source passed from a master through cassette, DAT and CDR, then converted to SHN [1]
